sources.entry: AI Gist - Local-first AI prompt manager with variable filling, Jinja templates, AI generation, and WebDAV/iCloud backup.

summary.one_liner: AI Gist is a privacy-first, local-first desktop and mobile app for organizing, filling, and AI-generating or refining reusable AI prompts.
summary.what_it_does: Lets users create prompt templates using {{variable}} placeholders, which the app detects and fills in at use time, with Jinja template support. Prompts can be viewed as cards, in a table, or by category, and filtered or organized by tags, categories, ratings, and favorites. Copying a prompt records it in usage history, and the README mentions several kinds of history for revisiting and improving prompts. An AI model can be connected (the README names local Ollama and LM Studio, plus online models such as OpenAI and DeepSeek) to generate prompts, rewrite them (for example, make them more specific), or extract variables automatically, with customizable system prompts. Data is stored locally by default, can be exported and imported (CSV export is mentioned), and can be backed up or restored via WebDAV or iCloud.
use_cases: Organizing a personal library of AI prompts
Filling variables into reusable prompt templates
Generating new prompts with a local or online AI model
Refining prompts with AI rewrites or automatic variable extraction
Syncing prompt data across devices via WebDAV or iCloud
notable: Local-first: data stays on the device by default and works without network access
Variable filling with {{variable}} syntax plus Jinja template support
AI features for generating, refining, and extracting variables from prompts, with local model options
Runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS, with Chinese, English, and Japanese UI
Multiple views (card, table, category/folder) and multiple history records
caveats: Chinese-language README; the English README is linked separately but was not provided
Distribution differs by platform: Microsoft Store, App Store, and Snap Store listings, plus direct downloads; older macOS builds need a terminal command to launch
Development setup (yarn dev, Xcode/Android Studio for mobile) requires toolchains beyond a simple install
